name: Hesperian-Eyot
description: Glacier upon glacier, blue-white and creaking, buried in places by nitrogen snow. The shell is broken in places by frozen methane lakes, and through those breaches the deep ocean breathes plumes of frost into the dark.

Thin air makes every breath a small transaction. Locals, when there are locals, move slowly and speak quietly, conserving everything. Carpet-flora blooms all at once after each rare rain, turning whole basins scarlet overnight.
Whoever abandoned the monolithic structures of unknown origin did so in order: power first, then data, then people. The airlocks were cycled from the inside, gently, one last time.
The charts mark this world in cautious amber. Those who ignore the marking tend to come back rich, changed, or not at all.
